quest.title: Neko Is a Cat: Shrine Cleanup
quest.description: Neko, "Provisional Head Priestess of the Asase Shrine," seems to have business with you...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Primogem x20, Mora x10000

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Nya, meow... That box has proven its worth indeed...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Ah, you return. The box you repaired has proved its efficacy quite well.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Not long after your departure, two humans in green came to the shrine, meow, meow.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Not only did they offer up some Mora, but the tall, green human seemed most excited to hear me speak. How easily startled you humans are, really...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Regardless, the Offering Box is a most wondrous artifact. Perhaps repairing another shall attract yet more people?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, that's not how that works...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Is that so? Human matters are so very bothersome.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: P—Paimon thinks this has got way more to do with the state of the shrine...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: And what of my shrine?

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Ho, is that so? Those little rascals quite enjoy playing amongst the piles of fallen leaves.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Ah, but if one yet recalls clearly, Hibiki used to use a long stick with pointy ends to build a pile of leaves. Now, if she did it, it must be the right thing to do.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: What would I know about the intricacies of human deeds? Still... if it were Hibiki...

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Hibiki often took that stick and waved it back and forth before the sun had risen. I used to enjoy chasing that stick, yes.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: But now that I am the provisional head priestess, such churlish behavior shall not do.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: I remember that Hibiki would also use water on the ground... an ill thing to do, really.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Domeki would come by at times as well, and he would use crossed metal plates to go snicker-snack! And the branches and leaves would come falling down.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: A very tall and loud human. He and Hibiki would play together a great deal.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Hmph. That rascal always chopped off the same branches that I loved most. An infuriating fellow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From the sound of it, they were doing cleanup. Guess you could call it re-organization as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sweeping the floor, washing it with water, and trimming the branches...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Such familiar work, eh...

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: So that was "cleanup," then? I understand. In that case, would you go forth and do as such?

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Ah, yes. You may forgo the snicker-snacking. I like the branches just the way they are.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: The long stick, leaves, and water will do. Have you understood my words?

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Meow! Yes, this work was given specifically to me by Hibiki. A vital task to be completed by no other.

choices.text: Actually, could I ask who Hibiki was?

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Hibiki is Hibiki. She is the head priestess of Asase Shrine.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And your name...

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: My name is Neko — a name bestowed by Hibiki.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: It was she who often came out to receive guests at the shrine, and so I was not obligated to manage such affairs.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: I had neither name nor title then. I slept where she wished, and played with whoever she willed.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: One day, Hibiki said that she would call me "Neko," on account of my habit of sleeping.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Hibiki is presently absent, but a shrine is no shrine without a head priestess, and so I have taken up that post.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: That is also why I hope to restore the shrine to its former liveliness before Hibiki returns.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: ...That's right! Once she returns, I can fall asleep in her bosom, and not have to wait for her to repair the Offering Box, or wait for her to use that long stick of hers to clear the leaves.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Well, I shall leave those tasks to you. There are some sneaky bugs that have stolen into the shrine, and they must now be driven out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Neko probably means trimming the branches.

choices.text: What exactly do you need done?

talks.objective: Clean the dirt around Asase Shrine

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Is your "cleanup" complete?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Everything's spick and span.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Meow, meow. That is good. I have also chased those little crawlies away.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Why, this shrine is looking more and more the part. The box is repaired, and the shrine itself is clean... Yes, more people shall surely come to pay their respects.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Meow, meow... We must return this shrine to its former glory, yes... Meow...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: We shall stop here. Thank you for your help thus far... meow, meow...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Speaking your language is... so tiring...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: I am going to rest. Perhaps your aid shall be required later also...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: When that time comes, do return here to... meow, meow...

choices.text: So, who used to tidy the shrine?

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: It was Hibiki. Domeki would help her sometimes, too.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Hibiki often took that stick and waved it back and forth before sunrise. She would also pour water on the ground. Ugh, water...

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Wait. Did she pour the water first? I do not quite recall the sequence of events...

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Domeki would come by at times as well, and he would use crossed metal plates to go snicker-snack! And the branches and leaves would come falling down.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: We must... return this shrine to its former glory, yes... Meow...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: When will Hibiki... finally return... meow...
